input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
input.rationale: Section 14.2.2 is PB's only convenience exit, but it fails the fallback on material terms: it is unavailable until SFJ has paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs, it closes entirely once the first Regulatory Approval is received, and the notice period is left blank ([***]) rather than set at 60-90 days. In a multi-year development term that is effectively no reliable customer convenience right. SFJ's exits (14.2.3 MAE, 14.2.5 bankruptcy, 14.2.6 Change of Control, 14.2.7 safety, 14.2.8.1 compliance breach, 14.2.9 Adverse Patent Impact, 14.2.10 JSC decision) are each trigger-based rather than at-will, so we have not treated them as vendor convenience rights; the redline confirms that position expressly. We targeted the preferred level because the fallback's three-months-of-fees cap has no analogue in this deal (the 300% Development Cost payment is consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package, not a subscription penalty) and we have left that buy-out economics untouched. Notice period ambiguity and the retained 300% buy-out are noted commercially, not separately redlined.

proposal.summary: Make PB's at-will termination unconditional on 30 days' notice with pro rata refund of prepayments, and bar SFJ convenience termination during the Term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need an unconditional exit right: as drafted, PB's at-will termination is available only after SFJ has spent $60 million and only before first Regulatory Approval, and the notice period is left blank. We have set it at thirty (30) days' notice with a pro rata refund of any PB prepayments, and confirmed SFJ has no convenience termination right during the Term.

ops.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
ops.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ, and SFJ will refund pro rata any fees or other amounts prepaid by PB for the period after the effective date of termination. SFJ has no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
